items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: So I went to work with Joe... So we got up and Joe and Oliver and Joe say, well, you sure surprised me... So we went seven nights a week over gardens.

ctx.x: So Bill, so Bill playing that corner, really was my life. I lived that life, I lived that life and I loved it. Well, what you really got yourself a reputation playing corner in New Orleans was playing in the brass bands, parades. On those parades, you met everybody and the corner players all had their cutting contests. So, I played in the brass band, in Black Penny's brass band with Louis, Renee and myself, regular. And later years, I worked with the Tuxedo band with Papa Celestan. That's where I got, come and…
They all went. They all went.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Lee and I were schoolmates too... I never would have lost his friendship... Lee and I attended school together.

ctx.x: Recall, Ellix. And then we got Lee Collins, he came up. And then Snagg Jones came up, he left, he had been playing with Celestan. And then comes Tommy Ladner. Tommy Ladner came up. So you just can see how it was with New Orleans musicians. And they were close knitted and they stuck together. And the guys said, oh this guy, they called him, called him Geechies, they called him Geechies, Cam Reed. And what they were wrong, you take people like Manny Perez, and Jimmy Noon, Eddie Atkins, and George Field, all those…
I understand Lee Collins couldn't read too well.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: The interviewee mentions Lee Collins in the context of Louis Armstrong defending him against Collins: 'Louis says, I put you in the band and you're going to stay in this band, I don't care what Collins said. And he and Collins had a big fuss.'

ctx.x: fights, he was the instructor back there.

Yeah, well he was a regular fashion player. Twenty-five or thirty suits of clothes. They'd give him suits of clothes just to advertise. I heard he died not so long ago in New York. And getting back to, well Lee played with Joe Oliver at the Lincoln Garden too, see? Well now the Sidewalk Blues, Lee wrote the Sidewalk Blues and Jellie Roten, turned it over to Jellie Roten and Jellie Roten had it to copyright it. And that was the last, that was the last, maybe Lee told you about it.
But Lee never did talk about it?
